steps.text: Question h42-r1.doors: the plan shows 1 door, the tour counted 2. The note says only: "Kitchen floor is wet along the walls. Power is on, fans can go in tomorrow." The agent called mark_wet with the quote "Kitchen floor is wet along the walls": true, but about water, not doors.
steps.title: Read the trace

steps.text: Every question got all seven tools. The model picked the edit it had evidence for, not the one the question asked about. The prompt said to answer the question; with a small model, a sentence in a prompt is a hope, not a rule.
steps.title: Find the cause

steps.text: 5 real questions became regression cases, including this one, a negation ("No water in the bedroom.") and a note about another room. tests/test_failure_fix.py fails if a rerun breaks any of them.
steps.title: Add the cases

steps.text: Each question now gets only its own tools and its own short prompt (a door question: add_door, no_change, ask_drafter). The guard that checks quotes also refuses an edit for the other question, so the drafter never sees one.
steps.title: Change the code, not the prompt

steps.text: The first rerun showed another weak-model habit: the model sometimes wrote its tool call as text instead of calling the tool, so the run ended with no valid answer. The runner now reminds it once. Runs with no valid answer: 13 before both fixes, 21 after. Regression case h27-r5.doors: still fails (ask drafter).
steps.title: A second habit, a second code fix

steps.text: Off-question answers 3 to 0; harmful edits 9 to 3; errors fixed 66 to 63 and missed 1 to 1 of 95; drafter items 138 to 147. h42-r1.doors now: ask drafter. The rerun repeats every model call: 30 of 191 answers that no fix targets also changed, which is the model's own variance.
steps.title: Before, after

failure_fix.summary: In the first full run, the agent answered 3 door questions with mark_wet: an edit for a different question. The drafter rejected each one, but each cost a review.
